Purpose: Places the method within the high-level hierarchy.
Identifies the named method or platform.
Summarizes the method in plain language.
Lists key status indicators or reference-point outputs.
Describes when the method is commonly applied.
Defines the minimum inputs needed for implementation.
Describes additional data that improve performance or interpretation.
Lists supporting information such as effort or related inputs.
Highlights representativeness, consistency and screening needs.
Specifies preparation steps before fitting or calculation.
Identifies whether indices or samples require standardization.
Documents how catches, ages or lengths should be grouped.
Explains whether fleets or gears should be split or combined.
Describes treatment of gaps and partial information.
Lists principal model parameters or derived quantities.
Documents fixed values, priors and externally supplied assumptions.
Describes whether the method is deterministic or includes observation and/or process error.
States whether latent process and observation components are separated explicitly.
Captures practical details relevant to coding or interpretation.
Summarizes the assumptions needed for valid interpretation.
Identifies parameters, inputs or settings to which results are most sensitive.
Highlights common ways the assumptions may be broken in practice.
Describes likely bias or misleading inference under assumption violation.
Lists simple indicators that the method may be unsuitable.
Lists data situations or configurations under which the method should not be applied.
Describes frequent ways the method is applied incorrectly and their consequences.
Minimum checks to pass before results are used for advice.
Concrete checks an app or analyst runs before fitting, with the action if a check fails (after Gutierrez and Kleisner, 2018).
States whether outputs support status only, indicator-based HCRs, catch advice or MSE.
Links to worked examples or comparative applications.
Provides primary literature and supporting documents.
Lists packages, templates or code resources.
